s: The tribes fight on after Joshua's death but fail to drive out all the Canaanites.
A new generation forgets the Lord. The cycle begins: sin, oppression, crying out, and God raising up judges.
The judges Othniel, Ehud and Shamgar deliver Israel.
Deborah, a prophetess, leads Barak against Sisera, and Jael kills Sisera.
The song of Deborah and Barak celebrates the victory.
Midian oppresses Israel. An angel calls Gideon, who tears down Baal's altar and asks for a sign with a fleece.
God reduces Gideon's army to three hundred men, and they rout Midian with trumpets and torches.
Gideon pursues the Midianite kings and refuses to be king, but makes an ephod that becomes a snare.
Abimelech, Gideon's son, murders his brothers and makes himself king, and comes to a violent end.
The judges Tola and Jair. Israel turns to idols, then repents.
Jephthah delivers Israel from Ammon but makes a rash vow concerning his daughter.
Ephraim quarrels with Jephthah. The judges Ibzan, Elon and Abdon.
An angel announces the birth of Samson, who is to be a Nazirite from birth.
Samson marries a Philistine woman and poses a riddle at the wedding.
Samson takes revenge on the Philistines and kills a thousand with a donkey's jawbone.
Delilah betrays Samson, who loses his strength when his hair is cut. In his death he pulls down the temple of Dagon.
Micah makes an idol and hires a Levite as his priest.
The tribe of Dan steals Micah's idol and priest and settles in the north.
A Levite's concubine is abused and killed at Gibeah in Benjamin.
Israel goes to war against Benjamin and nearly destroys it.
Wives are found for the surviving Benjaminites. In those days there was no king in Israel.
